Seeking Private Mental Health Training & Clinical Mentorship Memphis, TN

Hello, everyone!

My name is Shadonna Banks, and I am seeking an experienced LPC-MHSP, licensed psychologist or Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) in the Memphis area who offers private, individualized clinical training, mentorship and professional consultation.

I am currently completing my master’s degree in clinical Mental Health Counseling and already have an established clinical supervisor for my school and internship requirements. I am looking for additional professional development beyond my required supervision hours.

I would love to connect with someone who is willing to provide private, one-on-one teaching and hands-on training in areas such as:

Comprehensive mental health assessments and diagnostic interviewing
DSM-5-TR diagnosis and differential diagnosis
Individual psychotherapy, CBT and other evidence-based approaches
Treatment planning, clinical documentation and progress notes
Trauma-informed care, suicide risk assessment and crisis intervention
Co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders
Psychiatric evaluations, psychotropic medications and collaborative care
Case conceptualization, ethical decision-making and clinical consultation
Working with court-involved clients and individuals referred through federal programs
I am particularly interested in someone who enjoys teaching and is willing to offer structured private sessions, case discussions, practical exercises and opportunities to strengthen my clinical skills.

This is paid professional training and mentorship, not a request for internship placement or supervision hours.

I prefer in-person sessions in Memphis but am open to virtual training. I would love to establish an ongoing professional relationship with someone who can help me continue growing as a mental health professional.

If you provide this type of training or know someone who does, please send me a private message with your credentials, availability, areas of expertise and rates.

Thank you for your recommendations and referrals!

Shadonna Banks, 

LADAC I, Clinical Mental Health Counseling Graduate Student

Clinical Supervision

I offer clinical supervision for pre-licensed and developing clinicians seeking a space that honors the complexity of becoming a healer—not simply learning how to meet the requirements of a profession.

As a state-approved supervisor in Texas, Nevada, Missouri, and Illinois, I provide supervision that supports clinical development while creating space to thoughtfully explore Western psychotherapy alongside Indigenous, Eastern, somatic, spiritual, and other culturally rooted approaches to healing.

Supervision may include case conceptualization, clinical skill development, ethics and professional identity, documentation, boundaries, cultural humility, scope of practice, and navigating how spiritual or traditional healing frameworks intersect with licensed mental health practice.

My goal is not to teach clinicians to simply add Indigenous or spiritual practices to psychotherapy. It is to help clinicians develop the discernment to understand what belongs in clinical practice, what requires additional training or relationship, what should remain culturally or ceremonially distinct, and how to practice with respect and accountability.

Clinical & Integrative Consultation

For licensed clinicians, healers, and other helping professionals who do not need formal supervision, I also offer consultation for those navigating the intersection of psychotherapy, spirituality, culture, traditional healing, and integrative care.

This may be especially helpful for clinicians asking questions such as: How do I ethically incorporate spirituality into my work? How do I distinguish psychotherapy from traditional or ceremonial healing? What does culturally responsible integration actually look like? Where are the boundaries between my clinical license, personal spiritual practice, and other healing roles?

Consultation can include support around ethical integration, scope and boundaries, culturally grounded practice development, case consultation, somatic and experiential approaches, professional identity, and creating frameworks that honor multiple ways of knowing without appropriating traditions or misrepresenting one's training.

This space is particularly intended for clinicians who want to move beyond simply collecting techniques and instead develop a more intentional, relational, culturally humble approach to healing.

A Shared Philosophy

Whether you are seeking formal supervision or professional consultation, this work is grounded in the belief that Western psychotherapy does not represent the only way human beings have understood suffering, healing, relationship, and transformation.

We can learn from multiple healing traditions while also respecting their histories, cultural contexts, boundaries, and the communities from which they come.

Licensed and pre-licensed clinicians are welcome.

State-approved clinical supervision: Texas • Nevada • Missouri • Illinois
Consultation: Available to clinicians and helping professionals beyond these states, subject to applicable professional and jurisdictional requirements.

$300/month Full Access — 4 meetings per month

Schedule an initial fit meeting to explore whether supervision or consultation is the right fit for you.

Death is something that inevitably comes up in our work (as well as our personal lives!) but so many of us are uncomfortable talking about it. It is also a topic that is not often discussed in our schooling. How can we prepare ourselves better for conversations about death and end-of-life with our clients? How can we navigate our own discomfort around this topic while supporting those who need us?

Our upcoming CE program, The Art and Ethics of Talking about Death and Dying with Tova Jussim, LCSW-C will help you develop those essential skills - while earning 3 ethics CEs!

Early bird pricing ends October 1st. Group rates available.

And you shouldn’t have to become a credentialing or revenue-cycle expert just because you decided to grow your practice.

That’s what MendZak Consulting looks at.

Our Provider-to-Payment Milestone Analysis™ follows your provider from hire all the way to first payment to identify where the process is getting stuck and give you a clear roadmap for correcting it.

You focus on your clients.

If you work with **children or their parents**, you will see medical trauma come into your therapy room at some point. 

Medical trauma is one of those things that no one wants to think about, until it happens to them. 

But when it does happen, you want to be prepared, and this workshop is designed to prepare you.

Join us live on Thursday OR watch the replay as many times as you need in the future.

**Medical Trauma CE: When Healthcare Hurts - Supporting Children with Medical Trauma**

**PRESENTER:**

Sara Loftin LPC-S, RPT-S, who has worked in a pediatric hospital for over 13 years with children with medical trauma. She has presented on this topic at an international conference, and I'm so excited to welcome her into The Chronic Illness Therapist presenters! (To everyone who submitted their applications, thank you so much again, and we'll be reaching out soon to schedule you for future dates.)

**WHEN:**

September 24th | 1pm EST / 12pm CT / 11am MT / 10am PST

60-65 minutes
